answer: A trust-graph protocol restricts agent identities by routing random walks across a willow topology of signed peer endorsements. As verification queries wander through the network, an attestation lantern measures topological cut-capacities to isolate sparse Sybil clusters. An attacker incurs a non-amortizable cost in establishing scarce, authentic bilateral trust edges with established nodes. However, peripheral or newly initialized honest agents risk high false-positive rejection rates.
